courses.title: Grade 7 Life Science
courses.description: Build California Grade 7 life science understanding through cells, body systems, ecosystems, genetics, evolution, and biodiversity.

units.title: Cells and Living Systems
units.description: Start with cells as the basic unit of life and model how cell parts work together.

concepts.title: Cells and Living Things
concepts.description: Identify evidence that living things are made of cells and connect cell structures to basic functions.

concepts.title: Cell Specialization and Microscopy Evidence
concepts.description: Use microscope evidence and structure-function reasoning to explain how specialized cells support tissues and organs.

concepts.title: Cell Membrane and Materials Movement
concepts.description: Model how cell membranes help cells exchange materials while maintaining workable internal conditions.

units.title: Body Systems and Information Processing
units.description: Connect cells, tissues, organs, organ systems, and sensory responses.

concepts.title: Body Systems and Information Processing
concepts.description: Explain how body subsystems interact and how sensory receptors support responses and memories.

concepts.title: Homeostasis and Feedback in Body Systems
concepts.description: Model how receptors, signals, and interacting body systems help maintain workable internal conditions.

concepts.title: Digestion, Molecules, and Cell Fuel
concepts.description: Trace how digestive, circulatory, and cellular processes turn food into usable materials and energy access for cells.

units.title: Growth and Energy Flow
units.description: Study growth factors, photosynthesis, cellular respiration, and matter and energy in organisms.

concepts.title: Growth, Photosynthesis, and Cellular Respiration
concepts.description: Use evidence to connect growth factors, photosynthesis, cellular respiration, matter, and energy flow.

concepts.title: Matter and Energy Transfer in Organisms
concepts.description: Connect photosynthesis, respiration, food webs, matter cycling, and energy flow using evidence and models.

concepts.title: Water Transport and Transpiration
concepts.description: Connect roots, xylem, and leaves to water movement and evaluate evidence about plant water loss.

concepts.title: Investigating Photosynthesis
concepts.description: Use controlled comparisons, matter models, and rate data to investigate photosynthesis and distinguish oxygen production from net change.

units.title: Ecosystems
units.description: Explore how organisms interact with each other and with resources in ecosystems.

concepts.title: Ecosystem Interactions and Dynamics
concepts.description: Analyze patterns in populations, resources, food webs, and ecosystem changes.

concepts.title: Population Data and Ecosystem Stability
concepts.description: Interpret population data, resource limits, and food-web models to reason about ecosystem stability.

concepts.title: Energy Pyramids and Food Web Efficiency
concepts.description: Use energy pyramid and food-web models to explain why energy decreases at higher feeding levels.

concepts.title: Limiting Factors and Carrying Capacity
concepts.description: Interpret population data to explain how resources and limiting factors affect carrying capacity.

concepts.title: Decomposers and Matter Cycling
concepts.description: Trace matter through dead material, decomposers, air, soil, and plants using evidence and system boundaries.

concepts.title: Ecosystem Disturbance and Recovery
concepts.description: Use before-and-after data, food webs, and comparison sites to explain ecosystem responses to disturbance and evaluate recovery.

concepts.title: Competition and Resource Partitioning
concepts.description: Use resource-use models and controlled comparisons to explain competition and how differences in resource use can reduce overlap.

units.title: Genetics and Inheritance
units.description: Build models for heredity, chromosomes, genes, traits, and variation.

concepts.title: Genetics, Inheritance, and Variation
concepts.description: Model how genes and chromosomes influence inherited traits and variation.

concepts.title: DNA, Genes, Chromosomes, and Traits
concepts.description: Use models to connect DNA, genes, chromosomes, proteins, and observable traits without reducing genetics to memorized vocabulary.

units.title: Evolution and Earth/Life History
units.description: Use evidence from fossils, anatomy, DNA, and populations to reason about evolution.

concepts.title: Evolution Evidence and Life History
concepts.description: Interpret fossil and organism evidence to explain common ancestry and change over time.

concepts.title: Fossil Record and Rock Layer Evidence
concepts.description: Interpret fossil placement, rock layers, and anatomical patterns to reason about life history over time.

concepts.title: Natural Selection and Adaptation
concepts.description: Use scenarios and data to explain inherited variation, environmental pressures, adaptation, and population change.

concepts.title: Comparative Anatomy and Evolutionary Relationships
concepts.description: Compare body structures and hidden anatomical patterns to evaluate evidence for evolutionary relationships.

units.title: Biodiversity and Human Impact
units.description: Apply life science ideas to biodiversity, ecosystem services, and human design choices.

concepts.title: Biodiversity and Human Impact
concepts.description: Evaluate how biodiversity supports ecosystems and how people can reduce impacts with evidence-based solutions.

concepts.title: Biodiversity Solutions and Tradeoffs
concepts.description: Evaluate human-impact solutions using biodiversity data, constraints, tradeoffs, and evidence-based design reasoning.

concepts.title: Invasive Species and Food-Web Changes
concepts.description: Distinguish introduced species from harmful invaders, trace direct and indirect food-web effects, and evaluate evidence for management choices.
